name: Crimpshrine
label: Lookout!
lede: Two 13-year-olds started S.A.G. in 1982 with one drum and a three-string guitar. By 1989 the band, by then Crimpshrine, had a Lookout! EP, a US tour that came apart in Florida and a regular spot at 924 Gilman Street.

eras.title: One drum, three strings
eras.text: Aaron Cometbus and Jesse Michaels started the band at 13 with almost no gear, and Jeff Ott joined at 12. Michaels was out by 1984, and what was left took a new name.

years.big: "One drum and only three strings on the guitar."
years.p: That's how [[Aaron Cometbus|47e0c017-6e9e-408b-8c9e-e01950fb4892]] described the gear when he and [[Jesse Michaels|cf8b6e69-523c-4a64-b2e8-c64f171b742b]] started S.A.G. in the East Bay. [[Jeff Ott|64aea4ad-d055-4454-b023-bc3fcd0e2f9a]] joined at 12 on drums, then moved to guitar as Cometbus took the kit.
years.xp:
The three-string guitar was tuned to a barre chord. Michaels later said Ott was "twenty times better than us." Ott's own account of those first months is blunter: he "didn't know any chords, so I played with my thumb."

Michaels went on to sing in [[Operation Ivy|931e1d1f-6b2f-4ff8-9f70-aa537210cd46]]. Ott and Cometbus stayed together for seven years.

years.h: Jesse Michaels is out, and S.A.G. becomes Crimpshrine
years.p: Michaels is removed from the band in 1984. [[Jeff Ott|64aea4ad-d055-4454-b023-bc3fcd0e2f9a]] and [[Aaron Cometbus|47e0c017-6e9e-408b-8c9e-e01950fb4892]] rename it after a girl they knew with bleached, burned, crimped hair.
years.xp: Michaels has put his exit down to "smoking too much pot." The two left looked for a female singer first, then Ott took over vocals in late 1984, with Cometbus now on drums.

eras.title: Ott's basement, then Gilman
eras.text: The band rehearsed in Ott's basement while bass players came and went. Then Pete Rypins stuck, and the shows and the first tape followed.

years.cap: Jeff Ott and Aaron Cometbus with Dave Ed on bass at New Method, Emeryville, c. 1985
years.src: Wikipedia: Crimpshrine · Thrillhouse Records: Murray Bowles photos
years.h: Tim Armstrong, then called Lint, takes a turn on bass
years.p: [[Tim Armstrong|beaecc2d-20c7-4221-8fd2-682c82f0faab]], later of [[Operation Ivy|931e1d1f-6b2f-4ff8-9f70-aa537210cd46]] and [[Rancid|24f8d8a5-269b-475c-a1cb-792990b0b2ee]], is one of several bassists Crimpshrine tries in 1985.
years.xp:
It was a busy year for a band with no stable lineup. [[Jeff Ott|64aea4ad-d055-4454-b023-bc3fcd0e2f9a]] tried synthesizer and piano, and a violinist named Isaac sat in for a while.

The photo is from what a Murray Bowles photozine calls the first "real" Crimpshrine show, at New Method in Emeryville. According to Aaron Cometbus, they used the Canadian band the Asexuals' gear and played a few songs before the Asexuals. That's Dave Ed of Neurosis on bass.

years.cap: Flyer: Christ On Parade, Neurosis and Crimpshrine at The Place, Davis
years.h: Pete Rypins finally stays on bass
years.p: With [[Pete Rypins|ccab8147-c618-4a75-b3e9-99948336a03d]] in October, Crimpshrine settle into a trio with [[Jeff Ott|64aea4ad-d055-4454-b023-bc3fcd0e2f9a]] and [[Aaron Cometbus|47e0c017-6e9e-408b-8c9e-e01950fb4892]] and start playing places that aren't Ott's basement.

years.cap: Flyer: Crimpshrine and Operation Ivy at The Place, Davis, June 19, 1987
years.h: First demo, recorded at 924 Gilman Street
years.p: Crimpshrine tape the demo in February at the all-ages Berkeley club where the East Bay scene was taking shape.
years.xp: The band was already playing out by the summer. They shared a bill with [[Operation Ivy|931e1d1f-6b2f-4ff8-9f70-aa537210cd46]] in Davis on June 19, and two Gilman sets from June were filmed on VHS.

years.h: Maximumrocknroll asks, and the band cuts two songs
years.p: For the magazine's Turn It Around! compilation, Crimpshrine record "Another Day" and "Rearranged" in August.

years.h: Kevin Army records the debut EP at Dangerous Rhythm
years.p: In September the band cut Sleep, What's That? in Oakland. Its title track was inspired by Berkeley's Reaganville tent city, which police tore down in 1987.
years.xp:
The Reaganville camp was the "Homeless Liberation Front" encampment, which [[Jeff Ott|64aea4ad-d055-4454-b023-bc3fcd0e2f9a]] supported. "In My Mind" came from a different scene: a bus driver's callous response to an unresponsive Black passenger, which Ott read as unconscious racism.

He said people "must all strive to recognize and remove these small but very ingrained pieces of intolerance from ourselves."

eras.title: Sleep, then Florida
eras.text: The EP put Crimpshrine on Lookout! and on the East Bay map. Then the only US tour fell apart in Gainesville.

years.h: Sleep, What's That? comes out as Lookout LK 004
years.p: David Hayes's label presses 2,000 numbered copies on January 30, 1988, each with a red stamp.
years.xp:
A pressing-plant mistake put about 50 copies on blue marble vinyl. The original back cover carries a Laytonville address; by the 1991 pressing it read Berkeley, after Lookout moved there.

Wikipedia calls it "a classic Lookout Records release" and the band's strongest recording. It was out of print by 1992.

years.cap: Flyer: the Beatnigs, Fugazi, Crimpshrine and Yeastie Girls at Gilman Street, Berkeley, May 20, 1988
years.h: Idon Bryant makes Crimpshrine a four-piece
years.p: Soon after the EP, Idon Bryant joins on second guitar, the first time the band has had more than three people.
years.xp: The band recorded a debut album at Dancing Dog Studios in Emeryville that April, with the new lineup. Lookout turned the tapes down.

years.cap: Flyer: Crimpshrine, the Offspring, Nation On Fire and others at 924 Gilman, Berkeley, July 16, 1988
years.h: Rypins and Bryant quit mid-tour in Gainesville
years.p: On Crimpshrine's only US tour, [[Pete Rypins|ccab8147-c618-4a75-b3e9-99948336a03d]] and Idon Bryant walk out in Florida and leave [[Jeff Ott|64aea4ad-d055-4454-b023-bc3fcd0e2f9a]] and [[Aaron Cometbus|47e0c017-6e9e-408b-8c9e-e01950fb4892]] with no bassist.
years.xp:
[[Ben Weasel|bdce6736-8bc6-4818-8fd7-781822b674a9]] and John Jughead of [[Screeching Weasel|e4a135d0-1948-4620-bc07-b0217d09ccc1]] drove down from Chicago to help, and Weasel played bass for two shows.

The tour was in September 1988.

years.h: Paul Curran arrives with his brother and a Ford Pinto
years.p: [[Paul Curran|f8aa835d-258f-49e6-9ab0-6aa1ce074320]] takes over bass and finishes the tour, then stays through the band's last recordings.
years.xp: His brother Jack drove the Pinto. Jack Curran later formed [[Fifteen|51cb9a1a-cc3f-48e6-85c4-b0843fc7b697]] with Ott.

eras.title: Seven years end in May
eras.text: The last year brought one more EP, a record that only came out in Germany and two splits, then the end.

years.h: Quit Talkin' Claude... is the last EP
years.p: Recorded at Dancing Dog Studios in January, it's the last thing Crimpshrine release before the band ends.

years.h: Lookout passes, so a German label puts out Lame Gig Contest
years.p: Musical Tragedies in Germany releases the album, a mix of the rejected April 1988 session and earlier tracks.
years.xp: L.A. Weekly later named Lame Gig Contest one of the top five albums of pre-commercial pop punk, according to Wikipedia's Jeff Ott article.

years.h: Two splits, with Mutley Chix and with G-Whiz
years.p: The Mutley Chix split is Closed Up, Caught Up and Fucked Up; the G-Whiz one is Burning Bridges.
The split comes weeks after Quit Talkin' Claude... and seven years after S.A.G.'s one drum.
years.xp: [[Aaron Cometbus|47e0c017-6e9e-408b-8c9e-e01950fb4892]] went on to [[Pinhead Gunpowder|f7b3c394-3654-4bde-baea-32804f87fe24]] and [[Jeff Ott|64aea4ad-d055-4454-b023-bc3fcd0e2f9a]] to [[Fifteen|51cb9a1a-cc3f-48e6-85c4-b0843fc7b697]]. [[Paul Curran|f8aa835d-258f-49e6-9ab0-6aa1ce074320]] joined Monsula, and [[Pete Rypins|ccab8147-c618-4a75-b3e9-99948336a03d]] played in Tilt and later the Tantrums.

eras.title: Comps, a tribute and a documentary
eras.text: Collections, a split single and a tribute album kept the band in print. A documentary on the Gilman scene came in 2017.

years.src: Wikipedia: Sleep, What's That? · Wikipedia: Crimpshrine
years.h: The Sound of a New World Being Born collects the EP and more
years.p: The compilation gathers Sleep, What's That? and other Crimpshrine tracks after the original went out of print.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the compilation to 1998, not 1992. An earlier collection, Duct Tape Soup, did come out in 1992.

years.p: The split pairs Crimpshrine's "Better Half" with [[Jawbreaker|ec88cdc3-0517-4951-b5ef-7323e7316db0]]'s "Sanctuary."

years.h: Can You Spare a Dime? honors Crimpshrine and Fifteen
years.p: The tribute album from Microcosm Publishing covers both of Jeff Ott's bands.

years.h: Turn It Around puts the band on screen
years.p: The 2017 documentary Turn It Around: The Story of East Bay Punk covers the Gilman scene Crimpshrine played in.
